title: pH Formula

references.label: NCERT Chemistry Part II, Class 11 — Equilibrium

explanation: pH is defined as the negative base-10 logarithm of the molar hydrogen ion concentration. Because it's logarithmic, each single-unit change in pH corresponds to a tenfold change in [H⁺] — a frequently tested point. For strong acids/bases that fully dissociate, [H⁺] or [OH⁻] can be read directly from the given concentration; for weak acids/bases, an equilibrium (Ka/Kb) calculation is needed first.
conditions: pH + pOH = 14 relationship specifically holds at 25°C, where Kw = 10⁻¹⁴
commonMistakes: Applying pH = −log[H⁺] directly to a WEAK acid's total (analytical) concentration instead of first solving for the actual equilibrium [H⁺] using Ka.
Forgetting that a pH change of 1 unit is a 10-fold concentration change, not a 10% or additive change.
genZNote: pH is a logarithm cosplaying as a simple number — small digit changes hide big concentration swings underneath.
